author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Massachusetts has offered Insulet a potential incentive package worth more than $40 million as the medical-device maker considers a substantial expansion in Acton. The package would provide at least $40,000 in state tax credits for each qualifying new job, covering as many as 1,000 net full-time positions created through 2032.

Insulet, which makes the Omnipod insulin-delivery system, is headquartered in Acton and employs about 1,700 people in Massachusetts. The company has added roughly 200 employees in the state this year. Its preliminary plans include a $33 million renovation at 35 Nagog Park for approximately 500 to 530 workers, along with another $11 million to $12 million investment at 100 Nagog Park.

The offer is the largest single-company award in the history of the Massachusetts life-sciences tax incentive program, according to the report. Insulet has not made a final decision on the expansion, so the jobs and construction remain contingent on the company moving ahead and meeting the program’s requirements. The proposal reflects the state’s effort to retain growing life-sciences manufacturers while tying public support to job creation over several years.
dek: The medical-device maker is considering two Nagog Park investments and as many as 1,000 additional Massachusetts jobs through 2032.
headline: Massachusetts offers Insulet more than $40 million for Acton expansion
